entries.title: Proverbs 12:1
segments: True wisdom disposes men to seek instruction; and the want of wisdom leads them to hate reproof.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:4
segments:
A virtuous woman; a woman of worth, one who possesses both moral goodness and mental vigor. 
 
  She that maketh ashamed; by her baseness and worthlessness. 
 
  As rottenness in his bones; very painful and offensive.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:6
segments: Deliver them; from the wicked, who lie in wait for them.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:8
segments: Wisdom and folly will in the end find each its proper level.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:9
segments:
Despised, and hath a servant; occupying a humble station, yet living in a state of independence and comfort. 
 
None are more foolish and miserable than they who sacrifice comfort and independence to vain ostentation.  The affectation of wealth and rank makes men hypocritical and dishonest, and its end is ignominy and contempt.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:10
segments:
Regardeth the life; treats it kindly, and supplies it with needful food and rest. 
 
  Are cruel consist of cruelty; that is, in his heart cruelty takes the place of tender mercies. 
 
Kindness to animals is a characteristic of good men, as cruelty is of the wicked.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:11
segments: Vain persons; as Abimelech,
, Absalom,

, and others, who promise their followers plenty without toil. 
 
The divine ordinance is, that he who would have bread must earn it by the sweat of his brow; and it cannot be set aside by any ingenuity of man.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:12
segments: The net of evil men; the net which evil men use, for the sake of the prey which it takes.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:13
segments: Shall come out of trouble; his upright words shall deliver him.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:14
segments: Fruit of his mouth; the result of his wise and prudent discourse.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:15
segments: The who most need counsel are often least ready to receive it.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:16
segments:
Presently; immediately.  He vents his indignation upon the spot in passionate words and deeds. 
 
  Covereth shame; passes by shameful treatment in silence. 
 
When a wise man receives an injury, he pauses and considers the matter well before he speaks.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:17
segments:
He that speaketh truth; the man of truthful character. 
 
  Showeth forth righteousness; makes truthful statements, such as are in accordance with righteousness.  The proverb shows the agreement between men's character and their testimony.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:18
segments:
Is health; heals instead of wounds. 
 
No wounds are more painful than those which the calumniator inflicts upon his neighbor's good name.  He is an object of just abhorrence to God and man; but blessed is the tongue that is employed in healing strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:19
segments: Falsehood and duplicity promise ready success; but in the end they overthrow all who employ them.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:20
segments: Imagine evil; devise mischievous plans.  It is implied that their mischievous plans bring them into trouble.  See note to

entries.title: Proverbs 12:23
segments:
Concealeth knowledge; does not vauntingly display himself, or publish all he knows. 
 
  Proclaimeth foolishness; they have nothing in their heart to exhibit but folly, and they proclaim it everywhere, as if it were true wisdom. 
 
They who have the least wisdom are often the most forward to express their opinion.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:24
segments: It is an ordinance of heaven which none can reverse, that the idle shall be subject to the industrious.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:25
segments: The best medicine for soul and body is inward composure and cheerfulness; and this it is the Christian's duty and privilege to maintain; for in the midst of all his troubles and sorrows his heavenly Father has always "a good word" for him.

entries.title: Proverbs 12:27
segments: That which he took in hunting; that is, he takes nothing in hunting to roast.
